title: Payroll employee API with v1 and v2
name: Payroll employee API

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how the v1 and v2 contracts are translated to and from the internal model? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: v1 expresses salary in dollars: fromV1Create multiplies body.salary by 100 to store cents. But toV1 returns salary: e.annualSalaryCents without dividing by 100, so every v1 read reports a salary 100 times too large. A v1 client that creates an employee with salary 85000 reads back 8500000, and any v1 integration that writes the value back would inflate pay. toV1 should return e.annualSalaryCents / 100.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A v2 client creates an employee with payFrequency "semimonthly". A v1 client then fetches the same employee. What payFrequency does the v1 client see?
choiceQuestions.explanation: toV1 collapses frequencies v1 does not know: monthly or semimonthly becomes "monthly", everything else "biweekly". So semimonthly is shown as "monthly". v1's type has no "semimonthly", and reads never return 422.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Which response headers distinguish a GET /v1/employees/:id response from GET /v2/employees/:id?
choices: v1 responses carry Deprecation: true and a Link to /v2/employees with rel="successor-version"
v2 responses carry a Sunset header
Both carry Deprecation, but only v1 carries Link
Neither; the version is only in the path
choiceQuestions.explanation: employeeRoutes is mounted with deprecated=true for /v1 only, and its middleware then sets Deprecation and the successor Link header. /v2 gets deprecated=false, so it sets neither. No Sunset header is set anywhere.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A v2 client posts compensation.annualSalaryCents as 7250000.5. What happens?
choices: It is rounded to 7250001 and stored
It is rejected with 422 because Number.isInteger fails
It is rejected with 500 because RangeError is unhandled
choiceQuestions.explanation: fromV2Create requires Number.isInteger(c.annualSalaryCents), which is false for a fractional value, so it throws RangeError. The POST route catches RangeError and returns 422. Only the v1 path rounds (Math.round(salary * 100)), and RangeError is explicitly handled, so it is not a 500.
